Subject: Encryption & KMS: follow-up and next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so your security team has what they need: 

Summary of requirements you mentioned:
- Data classification: customer PII (names, emails, limited health metadata) stored in inference request payloads
- Retention policy: default 90 days, but you may need options for longer retention on archived requests
- Logging: request/response logging required for troubleshooting but must be configurable/redactable for PII
- Residency: primary requirement is US-only hosting (with potential EU consideration for future product lines)
- Encryption: in-transit and at-rest encryption required; preference for customer-managed keys (BYOK) if possible

What Redwood supports (high level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+, recommended TLS 1.3 for newer clients. Connections to our hosted API are always TLS-encrypted.
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption for all persisted data. Default keys are managed by Redwood.
- Customer-managed keys (KMS): we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for Hosted and Dedicated accounts. Keys can be rotated on your KMS schedule.
- HSM/managed HSM: for Dedicated or Private deployments we support HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM via KMIP) for FIPS/HSM compliance needs.
- Logging controls: request metadata (request_id, timestamp, model id, token counts) is always logged. Payload logging (request text/response) is configurable — we can redact, disable, or send to a customer-owned logging sink for audit.
- Region controls: Hosted API defaults to US regions; Dedicated/Private can be pinned to specific cloud regions or on-prem.

Attachments included: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope + controls), kms-options-matrix.xlsx (feature/ops/pricing comparison).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether Acme wants Redwood-managed keys or customer-managed KMS/BYOK.
2) If BYOK/HSM required, we’ll schedule a security deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer and Security Engineer to walk the integration flow, key lifecycle, and logging redaction capabilities.
3) I’ll send an initial mutual action plan and estimate for KMS/HSM add-on pricing (Ben will include pricing options).

Are you and your security contact available for a 45-minute call tomorrow or Thursday? Please send 2–3 windows that work.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our InfoSec team: 

1) Can you confirm if Redwood supports BYOK for the hosted offering (not just Dedicated)? We prefer keys we control in AWS KMS but may consider other options.
2) Key rotation: can we enforce a rotation policy from our KMS and will Redwood honor rotation TTLs without service disruption?
3) Logging: what exact fields are logged by default? We need to ensure PII payloads are not retained in plaintext in logs. Is payload redaction configurable per-route?
4) Retention windows: 90 days is fine for most, but we sometimes need 7 years for audit in healthcare. Can Redwood support longer retention for archive-only datasets? Any cost implications?
5) Data residency: you mentioned US regions by default — can you guarantee that data for this account and backup snapshots will remain in US regions only for hosted?

If you can provide short answers for the above, we can decide whether to push for BYOK for hosted or plan for a Dedicated/Private deployment. Also cc'd our security mailbox — they may add a couple of more technical questions.

Thanks,
Sarah

Hi Sarah —

Great questions — answering inline below and adding more detail on options so your team can pick the right path.

> 1) BYOK for hosted?
Short answer: Yes, with some caveats. For our hosted API we support customer-managed keys via the major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). That means you can create and control the keys in your cloud account and grant Redwood the minimum IAM/KMS permissions needed to encrypt/decrypt model artifacts and persisted blobs. For stricter HSM-backed controls we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments (see HSM note below).

> 2) Key rotation:
We support key rotation initiated from your KMS. Redwood is KMS-aware and resolves the current key version on each operation; key rotation in KMS will not cause downtime if the rotation is performed per the provider’s documented best practices. We also offer an optional validation step during rotation where our security engineer can walk through a rotation exercise with your team.

> 3) Logging: what fields are logged?
By default we log request metadata: request_id, account_id, timestamp, route, model, token_count, and basic latency metrics. Payloads (request text/response text) are only logged if account-level payload logging is enabled. For PII-sensitive workloads we have two options:
- Disable payload logging entirely for the account or for specific API keys/routes.
- Enable payload logging but configure automated redaction before persisting (e.g., PII tokens masked).
Both are configurable; we can demonstrate on the deep-dive call.

> 4) Retention windows: 90, 30, 365, 7+ years?
Default is 90 days. We support configurable retention policies per-account, with common presets (30/90/365). For multi-year archival (7+ years) we offer an archival add-on where flagged records are exported to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket under your control or retained in Redwood’s encrypted cold storage with additional compliance controls — there is an additional storage/retention fee for >365 days.

> 5) Data residency guarantee for hosted?
Hosted default is US regions; we can restrict your account to US-only physical regions and ensure backups/snapshots are stored in US regions only. For contractual guarantees (e.g., binding clause in agreement) we typically handle those in Dedicated/Private where you can pin exact cloud regions. We can provide a data residency statement and include it in the MSA.

HSM note: For FIPS/HSM requirements, Dedicated or Private deployments are the recommended path. We support CloudHSM (AWS) for Dedicated, and with Private deployments we can integrate with customer-managed on-prem HSMs via KMIP (for air-gapped scenarios).

Next steps I propose:
- Schedule a 45–60 minute security deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer (Ben) and Security Engineer. They will walk through BYOK flow, demonstrate rotation, and show redaction configs.
- If you confirm BYOK for hosted, we’ll start a runbook exchange (IAM roles, KMS ARNs, test key).
- I’ll attach the security architecture diagram and our SOC2 summary for your compliance team.

What times work for you and security? We have availability tomorrow 10–12 PT and Thursday 13–16 PT.

Best,
Marissa
